source_body.stem: A projectile has vertical velocity 12 m/s upward at t = 1 s. Take g = 10 m/s^2. What was its initial vertical velocity?

figure_semantics: one global time axis from launch to the stated event
source_contract.provenance_note: Synthetic golden fixture for production-kit validation; not a real examination source.

solution_steps: Use v_y = u_y - gt at the stated global time.
Rearrange to u_y = v_y + gt and evaluate to obtain 22 m/s.
verification_route: After one second gravity should have reduced the upward vertical velocity by 10 m/s.

first_step_reference: Place the stated event on the same clock that started at launch.

hint_seed.text: The stated time is measured from launch; do not reset the clock at the event.
Use the constant-gravity vertical-velocity model for one continuous projectile flight.
Start from v_y = u_y - gt and rearrange for the unknown launch component.

representation_stages: mark launch at t zero and the event at t one second
show the vertical velocity changing under downward gravity
